title: Two front vowels: /i/ and /ɪ/
goal: Practise /i/ and /ɪ/ and use it in a short, understandable exchange.
cue: For /i/, keep the tongue high and toward the front. For /ɪ/, let it sit a little lower and more relaxed. The difference is not only vowel length.
spelling: ee often represents /i/ and i often represents /ɪ/. These patterns have exceptions.
task: Ask for a seat and respond. Keep seat and sit distinct.
story: Ben sees a free seat. He sits by the window.
reviewPrompt: Return to day 3, 10, 14, 16. Recall a word or say one useful phrase before opening those lessons.

articulation.label: pit
articulation.alt: pit: /p/ → /ɪ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
/ɪ/: Front tongue, a little lower and relaxed.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.
